items.title: Clippy's Revenge
items.text:
Clippy's Revenge is a Windows tray app that lets Claude Code work with your classic Outlook. It runs a small MCP server on your own PC, talks to Outlook through COM, and keeps a local full-text index of your mail so searches are fast.

You can ask Claude things like "find the invoice Ann sent last month", "save the PDFs from that thread", "draft a reply", or "find a time next week when the five of us are free".

items.title: Why use it
items.text:
• No cloud. It uses the Outlook that is already signed in on your PC. There is no Microsoft Graph, no Entra app registration and no OAuth.
  • Fast search. Mail is indexed locally with SQLite full-text search, so Claude can search tens of thousands of emails without waiting for Outlook.
  • Works from WSL. Claude Code on Windows or in WSL connects over http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp.
  • You stay in control. See the promises below.

items.title: Safety promises
items.text:
What Clippy will not do

  • It never sends email. New mail and replies are saved as drafts only. You review and send them from Outlook.
  • It never deletes or moves your email.
  • The one thing that can send is a meeting invite, and only after you click Send in a confirmation dialog. You can set invites to "draft only" or turn them off.
  • It never starts Outlook by itself. Only the tray's Start Outlook item does, when you click it.
  • It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and every request needs a secret token.
  • Attachment contents are never indexed, only file names.

See the security model for details.

items.title: Where to go next
items.text:
1. Install with one line of PowerShell.
  2. Connect Claude Code by pasting one command.
  3. Browse the tools reference to see what Claude can do.

items.title: What you need
items.text:
• Windows 11
  • Classic Outlook (the one that opens OUTLOOK.EXE, not "new Outlook")
  • An Exchange or Microsoft 365 mailbox. IMAP/POP-only profiles are not supported.
  • Claude Code, on Windows or in WSL

items.title: AI drafts
items.text: Clippy's Revenge can write reply drafts for you, in your own writing style, using Claude. It is off by default. This page explains what it does, exactly what is sent to Claude, and how to set it up and fix it.

items.title: What it does and doesn't do
items.text:
• Drafts only. A reply is saved in your Drafts folder. Clippy never sends it. You read it, edit it and send it from Outlook.
  • Never deletes or moves mail. The only move is the new reply draft going into Drafts, the same as for reply_draft.
  • Reply subjects start with Re:: (double colon), like every reply draft. The model can't change the subject or the recipients. It can only choose reply or reply all.
  • Only new mail. It looks at mail that arrives in your Inbox after you turn it on, and never at mail older than the age limit (2 days by default). There is no backlog pass.
  • Your mailbox only, unless you turn on a shared mailbox one by one.
  • Not every email gets a draft. Newsletters, notifications, automatic mail and mail that needs no answer are skipped. See Rules.
  • Your signature is added, as for reply_draft.
  • Meeting times are added by Clippy from your calendar, never written by the model. See Meeting times.
  • Check every draft. The model can make mistakes. Where a reply needs a fact, such as a date or a number, it is told to leave a placeholder like [[date]] instead of inventing one.

When a pass creates drafts, the tray shows a balloon: "It looks like you got mail. I drafted 2 replies — they're in your Drafts folder." Click it to open Drafts.

items.title: Set up
items.text: You need one of two ways to reach Claude. Pick one in Settings, AI drafts.

items.title: Claude Code on this PC (default)
items.text:
Uses your own Claude Code, signed in with your Claude plan.

  1. Install Claude Code.
  2. Open a terminal, run claude and sign in. You sign in yourself. Clippy never signs in for you, never offers a claude.ai login, and never reads your Claude credentials. It only asks claude auth status --json whether you are signed in.
  3. In the tray, right-click, AI drafts, AI drafts settings.... Under Use, keep Claude Code on this PC (your Claude subscription) and press Check. The status line should show a check mark, for example ✓ Claude Code 2.1.323 · signed in (<sign-in method>).

Clippy runs claude headless, without a shell, with no tools for the model, and never with --bare. It finds claude.exe on your PATH, in %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin, or an npm install of Claude Code. Script shims (.cmd, .bat, .ps1) are never run. If yours is somewhere else, set Claude Code path to the full path of claude.exe.

items.title: Anthropic API key
items.text: Choose Anthropic API key, paste the key and press Save key. The key is stored encrypted with Windows DPAPI for your Windows user, is never shown again, and is never written to settings or logs. Remove key deletes it. Press Check: it reads the model from the API, which uses no tokens.

items.title: Model, effort and cost
items.text: The default model is Opus 5.5 at medium effort. You can change Model and Effort in the tab. Usage and cost come from your Claude plan or your API account, not from Clippy. Each email that Clippy evaluates is one Claude call, whether or not it ends up as a draft. Daily limit (default 30) caps the calls per day across all mailboxes. The tab shows Today: 3 of 30 Claude calls, 1 draft.

items.title: Turn it on
items.text: Check Draft replies to new email automatically in the tab, or use the tray menu item Draft replies automatically. The first time, Clippy asks for your consent. If Claude isn't ready, the tray opens the AI drafts tab so you can fix it first.

items.title: Consent and what is sent
items.text:
The first time you turn it on (and before the first manual draft), a dialog titled Turn on AI drafts? says:

Clippy will send new emails from your Inbox, earlier messages in the same thread, and samples of your sent mail to Claude (Anthropic) to write reply drafts in your style. Drafts are only saved, never sent. With Claude Code, this uses your Claude plan's usage. Shared mailboxes are included only if you turn them on one by one.

Buttons: Turn on and Cancel (the default).

While the feature is on, this leaves your PC for Anthropic, through Claude Code or the API:

What Details The email being answered Sender, recipients, date, subject and the full body including quoted history, cut at 20,000 characters Thread excerpts Up to 8 earlier messages of the same conversation from your local index, your own text only (quoted history and signatures cut), each cut at 4,000 characters Attachment names For the email and the thread messages. Names only Your name and address, today's date So the draft is addressed and dated correctly Your writing style guide The skill described below, which contains short examples of your sent mail with addresses, links and phone numbers removed. Its meeting-times section is left out About 150 to 300 samples of your sent mail Sent once a week, with addresses, links and phone numbers removed, to write the style guide

Never sent:

  • Attachment contents or any file.
  • Anything else from your index: other mail, your calendar (also for meeting times: free/busy is read by Clippy after Claude has answered), other folders.
  • Mail from shared mailboxes you haven't turned on.
  • Your Claude credentials. Clippy never reads them.

The model gets no tools. It can't read files, run commands, search your mail or call anything. Its answer is limited to: needs a reply or not, how sure it is, reply or reply all, and a short HTML body. A sanitizer then removes everything except plain formatting (paragraphs, line breaks, lists, bold, italic, underline, quotes), so links, images, styles and scripts never reach the draft. A prompt-injected email can at worst produce a bad draft, which you see before sending.

What Claude Code and Anthropic do with the data is governed by your Claude plan or API terms. See also Security.

items.title: Rules
items.text:
Before any email goes to Claude, cheap rules skip mail that needs no reply. The first rule that matches wins. No Claude call is made for skipped mail.

Skipped when Notes You sent it The sender is your own address No-reply sender noreply, no-reply, donotreply, mailer-daemon, postmaster, bounce and similar Automatic subject Starts with Automatic reply:, Autoreply:, Out of Office, Undeliverable:, Delivery Status Notification Never draft for Sender matches your exclusion list Only draft for The list isn't empty and the sender isn't on it Only when I'm in To or CC On by default. Your address isn't in To or CC. Mail sent to an alias address is skipped Already answered You or Clippy already replied, or a draft reply already exists Not normal mail Meeting requests, receipts, encrypted mail and similar Newsletters and lists List-Id, List-Unsubscribe or bulk Precedence headers Automatic mail An Auto-Submitted header other than no

Never draft for and Only draft for take one entry per line: an address (alex@example.org) or a domain (example.org or @example.org, which also covers subdomains). Each list holds up to 200 entries.

Then the model decides whether a reply is needed. It skips newsletters, FYIs, mail where you are only on CC and nothing is asked of you, and thank-you notes that close a conversation. A draft is saved only when its confidence reaches Minimum confidence.

Setting Default Model Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) Effort medium Daily limit 30 Claude calls Minimum confidence 0.6 Ignore mail older than 2 days Only when I'm in To or CC on Update weekly (writing style) on Offer meeting times when an email asks for a meeting on Number of times to offer 5 (1 to 10)

items.title: Limits and backoff
items.text:
• At the Daily limit, Clippy stops and continues the next day. The Activity window shows AI drafts: daily limit of 30 reached. I'll continue tomorrow.
  • When Claude's usage limit is reached, Clippy waits until the reset time if it knows it, otherwise an hour.
  • After other failures it retries after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and then 60 minutes, and gives up on a single email after 3 failed attempts.
  • Nothing happens while indexing is paused or Outlook isn't running.

items.title: Emails Clippy decides not to draft
items.text:
An email is decided once. When Claude says no reply is needed, or isn't confident enough, that email is not looked at again. Only emails whose Claude call failed are retried, up to 3 attempts.

When Claude is not confident enough, the Activity window shows a line, with the time the email was received and no subject, sender or text:

AI drafts: no draft for the email received 2026-11-13 14:05: Claude's confidence 0.55 is below your minimum of 0.60. To draft it anyway, select it in Outlook and use "Draft a reply to the selected email" in the tray menu, or lower Minimum confidence in Settings → AI drafts.

To get a draft for that email, select it in Outlook and use Draft a reply to the selected email, which skips the confidence check. Lowering Minimum confidence only affects mail that arrives afterwards; mail that was already decided is not reconsidered. The summary line after a pass counts these emails separately, for example AI drafts: 1 drafted, 2 low confidence (1.8 s), and the log shows the highest confidence seen against your minimum.

items.title: Shared mailboxes
items.text: Under Mailboxes in the tab, My mailbox is always on while AI drafts are on. Each shared mailbox you index has its own checkbox, off by default. Drafts for a shared mailbox use your own writing style.

items.title: Draft one reply now
items.text: Select one email in Outlook and choose Draft a reply to the selected email from the tray's AI drafts menu. This works even when automatic drafting is off, still needs your consent and a ready Claude, and counts toward the daily limit. It skips the rules and the confidence check, because you asked for it.

items.title: Meeting times
items.text:
When an email asks for or suggests a meeting or a call, the draft can offer concrete times from your calendar. Clippy computes them, not the model. The model only says that a meeting was asked for (and, if the email says so, how long it should be and in which time frame), and writes a short lead-in sentence in your style followed by a [[meeting_times]] placeholder. After the model has answered, Clippy reads Outlook free/busy and replaces the placeholder with the options. The model never sees or types a time, and your calendar is never sent to Claude.

Example, for a sender in Europe:

1. Tue 11/18  10:00–11:00 PT  (19:00–20:00 CET)
2. Wed 11/19  14:00–15:00 PT  (23:00–00:00 CET)

Outside European office hours:
3. Thu 11/20  08:00–09:00 PT  (17:00–18:00 CET)

Each option is one line, so you can delete the ones that don't suit before you send. The draft looks like this in Outlook: one option per line, with the columns kept aligned.

Who is checked. You, the sender, and, when the reply is a reply to all, everyone in To and CC (at most 10 other people, the sender first). People whose free/busy can't be read, for example people outside your organization, are left out of the check, so confirm with them yourself.

When and how long. From the start of the next day (or the earliest date the email names, if later) for 10 days, or until the latest date the email names, and never more than 60 days ahead. The length comes from the email and is 60 minutes when it doesn't say. Working hours, business days and whether tentative counts as busy come from Settings, Scheduling.

Ranking. The options are ranked by your calendar: times right before or after one of your meetings first (within 15 minutes, on the same day), then times next to a tentative meeting, then the rest, each group in date order. Free/busy can't tell a meeting from other busy time such as a focus block, so "next to a meeting" means "next to busy time". Within each free block, options start in 30-minute steps (plus one that ends exactly when the block ends), and they never overlap each other. At most Number of times to offer options are shown, both lists together.

Senders in Europe. For a sender who looks European, each option also shows the time in Central European time, always written CET, also in summer, when the actual offset is CEST. Options between 08:00 and 18:00 CET come first. If there aren't enough, the others follow in a second list headed Outside European office hours:. When the email is in another language, the model translates that heading. If you are in the CET zone yourself, or Windows has no Central European time zone, the CET part and the second list are left out.

Whether a sender is in Europe is guessed from two things: the time-zone offset in the email's Date header, and the country at the end of the sender's address (for example .de, .fr, .eu, .co.uk).

Date offset European country address (.de, .fr, ...) Other country address (.za, .jp, ...) .com, .org, .edu, ... +0100, +0200 Europe not Europe Europe +0000, +0300 Europe not Europe not Europe anything else not Europe not Europe not Europe none Europe not Europe not Europe

This is a guess and can be wrong:

  • Mail from inside your own Exchange organization has no such header, so only the address is used.
  • A European sender with a .com address in winter UK or Portugal time (+0000) or eastern summer time (+0300) isn't detected.
  • by, ru, tr, ge, am, az and kz addresses aren't counted as European.
  • A sender's mail program can write any offset.

If the guess is wrong, delete the CET part and the second list by hand, or ask Claude Code for times yourself (see the skill).

When Clippy can't offer times. The draft is still created, with a highlighted placeholder for you to fill in:

Placeholder Meaning [[add meeting times: no free time found between 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-25]] Nobody is free in that range. Check by hand [[add meeting times: Clippy couldn't read your calendar]] Your free/busy couldn't be read, for example Outlook was busy

When the sender proposes a specific time, the model doesn't accept or decline it. It leaves a placeholder such as [[check whether Tue 3 pm works]] and you still get the options. Like all placeholders, check these before sending.

Settings (Settings, AI drafts):

  • Offer meeting times when an email asks for a meeting: on by default. When off, drafts contain no meeting times and your calendar is not read.
  • Number of times to offer: 1 to 10, default 5.

This works in automatic passes and in Draft a reply to the selected email.

items.title: Your writing style
items.text:
Clippy learns your style from your own sent mail and keeps it in a Claude Code skill file, my-email-style.

  • It samples about 200 emails from the last 12 months of your Sent Items, a mix of internal and external, short and long, newest first, at most 3 per recipient.
  • It uses only your own text. Quoted history and signatures are cut, and automatic replies and meeting responses are left out.
  • Mail Clippy drafted for you is excluded, even after you edited and sent it. So are replies to mail that Clippy drafted an answer for, so the style doesn't learn from its own output.
  • Email addresses, links and phone numbers are replaced by <email>, <link> and <phone> before anything is sent to Claude, and again in Claude's answer.
  • It needs at least 20 suitable sent emails.
  • Clippy writes the file's header. Claude writes only the body: greetings and sign-offs, tone, length, formatting habits, phrases you use and avoid, and a few short examples.

Where the files are

File Purpose %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\my-email-style\SKILL.md The skill. Your copy to read and edit %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\my-email-style\SKILL.md Clippy's own copy of what it last wrote

The drafting prompt uses the file in .claude\skills, so your edits count.

Your edits are never overwritten automatically. If you changed the file (or you wrote a my-email-style skill yourself before), Clippy leaves it alone. Update weekly then does nothing, and the Activity window says writing style not updated: you edited it. Use Regenerate in Settings to replace it. Regenerate asks You edited your writing style skill. Replace your edits with a new version? with Replace and Keep mine (the default).

Refresh. With Update weekly on, Clippy creates the skill before the first drafting pass if there isn't one, and then refreshes it at most once every 7 days when at least 20 new sent emails have appeared. Style generation doesn't count toward the daily limit. In Settings you also have View (read-only), Regenerate (runs now and takes a few minutes) and Open in editor. The status reads Generated 2026-11-13 from 200 sent emails, Edited by you or Not generated yet.

items.title: The meeting-times section of the skill
items.text:
The end of SKILL.md always has a section, Offering meeting times, written by Clippy between the markers <!-- clippy:meeting-times v1 --> and <!-- /clippy:meeting-times -->. It teaches your interactive Claude Code sessions the same habit: to get times from find_free_times instead of making them up, to paste its offer_text unchanged, one option per line, and to set offer_cet when writing to someone in Europe. It also says to leave the options in the ranked order, to say that you will suggest times if none are found, and not to book anything unless you ask. A short paragraph on how you usually introduce meeting options is taken from your own sent mail.

  • A new or regenerated skill always gets the section.
  • A skill written before this feature gets the section added automatically, once, when Clippy starts, with no Claude call, as long as you haven't edited the file. The Activity window then shows writing style: added how to offer meeting times.
  • If you edited the skill, or wrote a my-email-style skill yourself, Clippy doesn't touch it. Regenerate replaces it, including the new section.
  • Changing anything inside the section counts as editing the file, like any other change.
  • The AI drafting prompt leaves the section out. It is meant for Claude Code sessions with tools, not for drafting.

Security note: this skill is also loaded by Claude Code

%USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\my-email-style\SKILL.md is a user-level Claude Code skill. That means your interactive Claude Code sessions, the ones with tools, can load it. It is the one place where text derived from mail reaches a Claude session that has tools. The file is model output based on your sent mail, so treat it with care.

What limits the risk: only your own text is sampled (quoted mail from other people is cut), addresses, links and phone numbers are removed from the samples and from the result, the prompt treats the samples as data and never as instructions, and Clippy writes the file header itself.

You stay in control: View or Open in editor shows the file, you can edit it, and you can delete %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\my-email-style at any time. Clippy then falls back to its own copy in %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge and, if you delete that too, to the plain style "write plainly, briefly and politely" until you press Regenerate. If you don't want the skill visible to your Claude Code sessions, delete the folder in .claude\skills after each update.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
The status line under Use and the Activity window tell you what is wrong. Fix it, then press Check.

Message What to do ✗ Claude Code wasn't found. Install it from https://claude.com/claude-code, sign in once in a terminal, then press Check. Install Claude Code, or set Claude Code path to claude.exe. A .cmd or .ps1 shim isn't supported ✗ Claude Code <version> is too old for AI drafts. Run "claude update", then press Check. Run claude update in a terminal ✗ Claude Code is installed but not signed in. Open a terminal, run claude and sign in, then press Check. Run claude and sign in yourself. Clippy can't do it ✗ Claude Code didn't answer (version) and similar (help, auth status) Press Check again. If it repeats, run claude --version in a terminal ✓ Claude Code <version> · signed in (...) plus · update Claude Code for best results Works. Updating lets Clippy keep your own CLAUDE.md, hooks and plugins out of drafting calls ✗ No API key saved. Paste your key and press Save key ✗ The API key was rejected (HTTP 401). The key is wrong or revoked. Save a new one ✗ The model "<model>" isn't available with this key. Change Model ✗ api.anthropic.com didn't answer. Check your network and try again AI drafts: Claude isn't signed in (Activity, error state) Sign in again in a terminal, then press Check. Drafting resumes AI drafts: Claude's usage limit was reached. I'll try again at 14:05. Wait. It retries by itself AI drafts: a Claude call failed (<kind>). I'll try again in 4 min. Usually temporary. If it keeps failing, press Check AI drafts: daily limit of 30 reached. I'll continue tomorrow. Raise Daily limit or wait AI drafts: no draft for the email received ...: Claude's confidence 0.55 is below your minimum of 0.60. Draft it by hand from the tray, or lower Minimum confidence. See Emails Clippy decides not to draft [[add meeting times: ...]] in a draft Clippy couldn't offer times. See Meeting times AI drafts: a reply draft couldn't be saved in Outlook. I'll try again later. Check that Outlook is running and Drafts is available Select one email in Outlook first. Manual draft: select one email That email isn't in your mailbox or an enabled shared mailbox. Manual draft: turn the shared mailbox on first Claude isn't ready: ... Manual draft: fix the status shown, then try again I couldn't draft that reply: ... The reason follows, for example Claude's usage limit, or that Outlook isn't running AI drafts need the email index, which couldn't be opened. Check the tray icon for the reason. The index failed to open. See Troubleshooting Clippy doesn't know your email address yet. Start Outlook, wait for the first sync, then try again. Needed to write the style. Start Outlook and let it sync Only 12 sent emails found. Clippy needs 20. Not enough sent mail to learn from yet There is no writing style skill yet. Press Regenerate to create one. Press Regenerate

If an email gets no draft, the usual reasons are: it arrived before you turned AI drafts on, it is older than the age limit, it matched a rule, or Claude decided no reply was needed or wasn't confident enough (the Activity window says so\nin the second case).

Logs and the Activity window never contain mail text, prompts, the style skill or Claude's answers.

items.title: Calendar and meetings
items.text: Three tools work with your calendar: list_events, find_free_times and send_meeting_invite. They read Outlook live, so Outlook must be running.

items.title: Listing events
items.text: list_events returns events in a window, with recurring events expanded, at most 500. Without arguments it covers the next 7 days. Pass mailbox to read a shared mailbox's calendar.

items.title: Finding a free time
items.text:
find_free_times reads Outlook free/busy for you and the attendees, combines it with your working hours, and suggests the first free blocks that are long enough. Nothing is booked.

A typical flow:

  1. You paste a list of attendees, as copied from an Outlook address line.
  2. Claude calls find_free_times and shows suggestions such as 1. Tue 10/15 1-3 PT.
  3. You say "book number 2". Claude passes that suggestion's start and end to send_meeting_invite.

Things to know:

  • People whose free/busy can't be read, such as people outside your Exchange organization, are listed as unknown and ignored. Check with them yourself.
  • Working hours, business-days-only, the time-zone label and whether tentative counts as busy come from Settings, Scheduling. Claude can override the hours and business days per call.
  • Suggestions are whole free blocks, in local time. They are ranked: times right before or after your own meetings come first, then times next to tentative meetings, then the rest.
  • Besides the blocks, the result has offers of exactly the meeting length and an offer_text with one option per line, ready to paste into an email. For someone in Europe, Claude sets offer_cet and each line also shows the time in CET, with the options inside European office hours first. See find_free_times.
  • Clippy's AI drafts use the same offers when an email asks for a meeting.

items.title: Meeting invites
items.text:
send_meeting_invite is the only tool that can send anything. Its behavior depends on the mode you choose in Settings, Scheduling.

Mode What happens Send (default) A confirmation dialog opens. The invite goes out only if you click Send Draft only The meeting is saved in your calendar, unsent. You send it from Outlook Disabled The tool refuses. Claude is told to ask you to enable it

Before anything is created, every recipient must resolve in Outlook. If one doesn't, nothing is created.

items.title: The confirmation dialog
items.text:
In Send mode a small window opens on top of your other windows without taking keyboard focus, and the tray icon turns amber. It shows:

  • who organizes the meeting (you, or a shared mailbox)
  • the subject, time, location and whether a Teams meeting was requested
  • the full recipient list, with people outside your organization highlighted
  • the invite body

You have three buttons:

  • Send sends the invite at once.
  • Save as draft saves the meeting in your calendar, unsent.
  • Cancel creates nothing. It is the default button and Esc triggers it, so pressing Enter never sends.

A countdown shows the time left (default 120 seconds; change it in Settings). If it runs out, the meeting is saved as a draft, not sent. Closing the window with the X counts as Cancel. Requests queue up, and only one dialog is shown at a time.

Every outcome appears in bold in the Activity window.

items.title: Teams links
items.text: Clippy can't add a Teams link. If Claude asks for one, the meeting is created without it and the result says so. Open the meeting in Outlook and click Teams Meeting.

items.title: Shared mailboxes
items.text: With mailbox, the meeting is organized from that shared mailbox's calendar, and free/busy checks include that mailbox instead of yours.

items.title: Changelog
items.text: The full list of releases, with downloads, is on GitHub.

items.title: v0.0.7
items.text:
2026-11-14

  • Meeting times: find_free_times now ranks its suggestions by your calendar (times next to your meetings first, then next to tentative ones) and returns offers of exactly the meeting length plus a ready-to-paste offer_text, one option per line. New offer_cet option adds the time in CET and puts European office hours first, with the others under "Outside European office hours:".
  • AI drafts offer meeting times: when an email asks for a meeting, the draft gets options from your calendar, computed by Clippy, not by the model. Two new settings, Offer meeting times when an email asks for a meeting and Number of times to offer. See Meeting times.
  • The writing-style skill has a new section, "Offering meeting times", so Claude Code offers times the same way. Unedited skills get it automatically at the next start.
  • New tool email_stats: counts mail by sender, domain, recipient, folder, month, week, weekday or hour in one call. Counts and names only.
  • New tool query_index: one read-only SELECT over the views mail, mail_fts and mail_attachments, with full-text search and snippets. See Tools reference and Security.
  • AI drafts: an email Claude isn't confident enough about now shows a line in the Activity window with how to draft it anyway, and the pass summary counts "low confidence" separately.
  • Privacy fix: the log no longer contains the text of tool error messages, which could quote search text or SQL back. Only the kind of error is logged.

items.title: v0.0.6
items.text:
2026-11-13

  • Auto-update: the installed copy checks GitHub once a week and installs a newer full release at its next start. The download is checked against the release's SHA-256 and rolled back if the new version doesn't start. Set Settings, General, Updates to Install automatically (default), Only tell me or Don't check. See Updates.
  • New About Clippy's Revenge… window in the tray menu: version, update status, Check for updates, Update now and links to the documentation and release notes.
  • New balloons for a newer version, a finished update and a rollback.

items.title: v0.0.5
items.text:
2026-11-13

  • AI drafts: Clippy can draft replies to new mail in your writing style with Claude Code or an Anthropic API key. Off by default, asks for consent, saves drafts only, never sends, and the model gets no tools. See AI drafts.
  • Writing-style skill built from your own sent mail, saved as my-email-style in your Claude Code skills folder. Your edits are never overwritten automatically.
  • New tray submenu AI drafts and a Settings tab with the same name.

items.title: v0.0.2
items.text:
Released as a full (latest) release, so the installer and releases/latest links pick it up.

  • The installer and the README use the releases/latest download.
  • One-line install: paste irm ... | iex into PowerShell.
  • install.ps1 -WhatIf downloads and verifies the release without installing.
  • Never deletes email: this is now a documented hard rule, checked by a test that scans the source.
  • Reconcile refuses mass deletes from the index when Outlook's ids don't match the index.

items.title: v0.0.1
items.text:
First release.

  • Tray app with a local MCP server on 127.0.0.1, protected by a bearer token.
  • Local SQLite full-text index of your mailbox and shared mailboxes.
  • Tools: search_emails, get_message, get_attachment, save_attachments, create_draft, reply_draft, list_events, find_free_times, send_meeting_invite and index_status.
  • Tray menu, Settings and Activity windows, and a confirmation dialog for meeting invites.
  • install.ps1 installer and uninstaller.

items.title: Connect Claude Code
items.text: Clippy's Revenge serves MCP over streamable HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp. The default port is 8765. Every request needs a bearer token that the app creates on first run.

items.title: Add the server
items.text:
1. Right-click the paperclip in the system tray.
  2. Choose Copy "claude mcp add" command.
  3. Paste it into a terminal where Claude Code runs (Windows or WSL).

The command looks like this:

claude mcp add --scope user --transport http clippy http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Then start Claude Code and run /mcp to check that clippy is connected.

Tip

Settings, Connection has the same command, a Test connection button and the token. The command box hides the token until you press Show; Copy always copies the full command.

If you change the port or regenerate the token, run the new claude mcp add command again. The app warns you before either change.

items.title: From WSL
items.text:
In WSL2's default NAT mode, WSL cannot reach the Windows host's 127.0.0.1. Use mirrored networking (Windows 11 22H2 or later). In %USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig on Windows:

[wsl2]
networkingMode=mirrored

Then run this in Windows and reopen your WSL shell:

wsl --shutdown

Check from WSL:

curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp     # expect: 401 Unauthorized

A 401 means the server is reachable and wants a token. Then paste the claude mcp add command in WSL.

The app listens on 127.0.0.1 only. It does not bind to the WSL virtual adapter, and it has no dependency on WSL interop: WSL talks to it over TCP.

items.title: Check that it works
items.text:
In Claude Code, try:

Use the clippy index_status tool and tell me how many emails are indexed.

Right after install the index is still filling. Recent mail becomes searchable first. See Indexing and search.

items.title: Rotate the token
items.text: Use the tray menu item Regenerate auth token…. The old token stops working at once, so you must add the server to Claude Code again with the new command.

items.title: Does it work with the new Outlook?
items.text: No. It needs classic Outlook, because it drives Outlook through COM. The new Outlook has no COM interface.

items.title: Does it work with IMAP or POP accounts?
items.text: Not supported. An Exchange or Microsoft 365 mailbox is required.

items.title: Can it send email?
items.text: No. It saves drafts and you send them from Outlook. The only thing that can send is a meeting invite, and only after you click Send in a confirmation dialog, unless you set invites to draft only or off.

items.title: Can it delete or move my mail?
items.text: No. It never deletes or moves email.

items.title: Why do reply subjects start with "Re::"?
items.text: It is intentional. Reply drafts always start with Re:: (double colon).

items.title: Can it write replies for me?
items.text: Yes, if you turn on AI drafts. Clippy then asks Claude to draft replies to new mail in your style and saves them in Drafts. It never sends them. It is off by default and asks for your consent first.

items.title: Will the AI draft offer meeting times?
items.text: Yes, when an email asks for a meeting and Offer meeting times when an email asks for a meeting is on (the default). Clippy picks the times from your calendar itself, the model never sees them, and each option is its own line that you can delete. For senders in Europe it adds the time in CET. See Meeting times.

items.title: Why does a meeting time say CET in summer?
items.text: The label is always "CET" for Central European time, also while Europe is on summer time. The time itself uses the real offset (+02:00 in summer), so the number is right.

items.title: Why did a draft come out without a CET time for a sender in Europe?
items.text: Clippy guesses where the sender is from the Date header and the address ending, and can miss, for example for a .com address in winter UK time. See Senders in Europe. You can add or delete the CET part by hand.

items.title: An email got no draft and the Activity window says "low confidence". What now?
items.text: Claude wasn't sure enough that a reply was needed, below your Minimum confidence. Such an email is decided once and not retried. To get a draft anyway, select the email in Outlook and use Draft a reply to the selected email in the tray menu. See Emails Clippy decides not to draft.

items.title: Does AI drafting send my mail to Anthropic?
items.text: Yes, while it is on: the email being answered, thread excerpts, attachment names and your style guide go to Claude through your own Claude Code (or your API key). Attachment contents never do. See what is sent.

items.title: Does Clippy sign in to Claude or read my Claude login?
items.text: No. You sign in to Claude Code yourself in a terminal, and Clippy only asks it whether you are signed in. It never reads Claude Code's stored credentials.

items.title: Why didn't a mail get a draft?
items.text: It may have arrived before you turned AI drafts on, be older than the age limit, be a newsletter or automatic mail, match a never-draft rule, or not need a reply. See Rules.

items.title: Is the writing-style file safe?
items.text: It is a Claude Code skill in %USERPROFILE%.claude\skills\my-email-style, so your interactive Claude Code sessions can load it. Review, edit or delete it any time. See the security note.

items.title: Does my mail go to the cloud?
items.text: Clippy has no cloud component. It runs on your PC and listens on 127.0.0.1. What Claude Code then sends to its model is the text of the mail it reads, so treat that as you would any use of an AI assistant with your mail. The optional AI drafts feature also sends mail to Claude, with your consent.

items.title: Do I need an app registration or admin consent?
items.text: No. There is no Graph API, Entra app registration or OAuth. If Outlook can open the mail, Clippy can use it.

items.title: Can Claude answer "who emails me the most?" or "how much mail do I get per month?"
items.text: Yes, in one call. Ask in plain language, for example "top 10 people who emailed me in the last year, with counts" or "mail per month since January". Claude uses email_stats, which counts mail in the local index by sender, sender domain, recipient, folder, month, week, weekday or hour. It returns counts and names, never mail text, and works while Outlook is closed.

items.title: Can Claude run its own searches with SQL?
items.text: Yes, with query_index: one read-only SELECT over three views of the index, including full-text search with snippets. Nothing can be changed and nothing outside those views can be read. See Security.

items.title: Does Outlook have to be running?
items.text: For indexing, yes. Clippy never starts Outlook on its own. Searching the existing index works while Outlook is closed. Tools that read live from Outlook (full messages not yet indexed, attachments, drafts, calendar) need it running.

items.title: Can Claude Code in WSL use it?
items.text: Yes, with WSL's mirrored networking. See Connect Claude Code.

items.title: Can other computers or web pages reach it?
items.text: No. It binds to 127.0.0.1 only, requires a token, and rejects any request that has an Origin header.

items.title: How far back does search go?
items.text: 12 months by default. Change it in Settings, Index (1 to 120 months).

items.title: Are attachments searchable?
items.text: Attachment file names are searchable. Their contents are never indexed. To read an attachment, Claude saves it with get_attachment and reads the file.

items.title: Where does it save attachments?
items.text: %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Clippy's Revenge by default. Claude can only save to allowed folders, which you control in Settings, General.

items.title: Can I use a shared mailbox?
items.text: Yes. Check it under tray, Shared mailboxes. See Shared mailboxes.

items.title: Does it start with Windows?
items.text: Yes by default. Turn it off with the Start with Windows item in the tray menu.

items.title: How do I update?
items.text: By default Clippy checks GitHub once a week and installs a newer version at its next start. To update at once, open About Clippy's Revenge… in the tray and press Update now, or run the install one-liner again. See Updates and Install.

items.title: How do I turn updates off?
items.text: Settings, General, Updates: choose Don't check (no automatic checks) or Only tell me (a balloon, no download). See Updates.

items.title: Does Clippy send anything to GitHub?
items.text: Only the weekly update check and the download, as plain requests that carry just the version number. No mail, no settings, no telemetry. See what is sent.

items.title: How do I uninstall?
items.text: See Uninstall.

items.title: Why does SmartScreen warn me?
items.text: The exe is not code-signed yet. The installer verifies its checksum.

items.title: Where are the logs?
items.text: %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\logs. Use the tray's Open log folder.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Clippy keeps a local SQLite database with full-text search (FTS5) of your mail. Claude's searches run against this database, so they are fast and still work while Outlook is busy. Full messages and attachments are fetched live from Outlook when needed.

Indexing needs Outlook to be running. Clippy attaches to a running Outlook and never starts it. If Outlook isn't running, indexing waits.

What is indexed: subject, body, sender, recipients, dates, folder, read state and attachment file names. Attachment contents are never indexed.

items.title: First run: backfill
items.text:
On the first run, Clippy reads your mail from the retention cutoff up to now, newest first, so recent mail becomes searchable first. The tray icon is blue and animated, and the tooltip shows progress such as indexing Inbox 1,240 / 8,000 (2025-11 → now). If you quit in the middle, it resumes where it stopped.

Ask Claude to use index_status to see whether the backfill is complete.

items.title: What is indexed
items.text:
Setting Default Where Retention 12 months (1 to 120) Settings, Index Folders Inbox and Sent Items Settings, Index Sync interval 5 minutes (30 s to 1 h) Settings, Index

Retention. Raising it starts a new backfill for the older mail. Lowering it removes older mail from the index right away. This only affects Clippy's index, never your mailbox.

Folders. Pick any folders in the Settings tree. Subfolders are separate entries, and a search for folder="inbox" does not include subfolders.

items.title: Keeping up to date
items.text:
Every sync interval (and when you click Sync now), Clippy picks up new and changed mail, then removes mail past the retention cutoff from its index.

Once a day for each folder, a reconcile pass compares the index with Outlook. It adds missing mail, refreshes read/unread state, and removes index rows for mail that is gone from Outlook. Reconcile only touches the index. As a safety measure, it refuses to delete rows when Outlook returns nothing, when none of its ids match the index, or when it would drop more than half of the index and at least 20 rows.

items.title: Pause, sync now and rebuild
items.text:
• Pause indexing stops the current cycle at the next batch. Batches that are finished are kept.
  • Sync now runs a cycle immediately.
  • Rebuild index… deletes the index database for your mailbox or for all mailboxes and starts again from scratch. Search finds less until it finishes. Use it if results look wrong. It never changes your mail.

items.title: Shared mailboxes
items.text:
Exchange mailboxes mounted in your Outlook profile (shared or additional mailboxes) appear under the tray menu Shared mailboxes.

  • Check one to start indexing it into its own database file.
  • Uncheck one to stop. You choose Delete its index, Keep index file or Cancel.
  • Each shared mailbox can have its own folders and retention in Settings, Index.
  • If Outlook isn't running, the list shows only configured mailboxes.

Tools use a shared mailbox with mailbox="helpdesk@example.com", or search all enabled ones with mailbox="all".

items.title: Search tips
items.text:
You rarely write queries yourself, but these are what Claude can use in query:

Query Meaning budget report Both words (AND) budget OR forecast Either word "annual review" The exact phrase proj* Words starting with proj

Filters such as sender, subject, date_from and attachment_ext narrow the results. See the search_emails reference.

items.title: Where the index lives
items.text: One database per mailbox in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\: index.db for your mailbox and index-<address>.db for each shared mailbox. It holds message bodies as plain text, like Outlook's own cache file. See index at rest.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Windows 11 with classic Outlook (not the new Outlook), signed in.
  • An Exchange or Microsoft 365 mailbox. IMAP/POP-only profiles are not supported.
  • No administrator rights are needed.

items.title: Install or update
items.text:
Paste this into PowerShell:

irm https://github.com/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex

The script downloads the latest release, checks ClippysRevenge.exe against the release's SHA256SUMS.txt, installs it and starts it. Run the same line again to update.

Clippy also updates itself once a week by default, so you only need the line above to install, to update at once, or to repair a broken install. To change how Clippy updates, see Settings, General, Updates.

It installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ClippysRevenge\, adds a Start menu shortcut called "Clippy's Revenge", and starts the app. A paperclip appears in the system tray. The app is set to start with Windows (you can turn that off in the tray menu or in Settings).

SmartScreen

The exe is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen warns the first time it runs. Choose More info, then Run anyway. The installer verifies the SHA-256 checksum of the download before it installs anything.

items.title: Preview first with -WhatIf
items.text:
-WhatIf downloads and verifies the release but changes nothing on your PC:

& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://github.com/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/latest/download/install.ps1))) -WhatIf

items.title: Install from a file
items.text:
Download install.ps1 from the latest release and run it:

.\install.ps1                                # same as the one-liner
.\install.ps1 -Source .\ClippysRevenge.exe   # install a local build instead
.\install.ps1 -NoStart                       # install but don't launch

You can also download ClippysRevenge.exe from the release and run it directly.

Option Meaning -Source <path> Install a local ClippysRevenge.exe instead of downloading -NoStart Don't start the app after installing -WhatIf Show what would happen; on the download path, download and verify only -Uninstall Remove the app (see below) -Purge With -Uninstall: also delete settings, token, index and logs, without asking

items.title: Uninstall
items.text:
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://github.com/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/latest/download/install.ps1))) -Uninstall

This stops the app and removes the exe, the Start menu shortcut and the "Start with Windows" entry. It then asks whether to delete your settings, token, index and logs. Add -Purge to delete them without asking. If you answer no, they stay on disk.

items.title: What gets stored where
items.text: What Where Program %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ClippysRevenge\ClippysRevenge.exe Settings and token %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\ Index and logs %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\ Saved attachments %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Clippy's Revenge

items.title: Next step
items.text: Connect Claude Code.

items.title: Security model
items.text: Clippy's Revenge gives an AI tool access to your mail, so it is built to do as little as possible and to keep that access on your PC.

items.title: What it never does
items.text:
• Never sends email. Drafts are only saved. You send them from Outlook. The one exception is a meeting invite, which is sent only after you click Send in a confirmation dialog.
  • Never deletes or moves email. The only move is putting a reply draft it just created into Drafts. Retention and reconcile remove rows from Clippy's own index only, never from your mailbox.
  • Never starts Outlook on its own. It attaches to a running Outlook. The tray's Start Outlook item, which you click yourself, is the only exception.
  • Never uses the cloud. No Microsoft Graph, no Entra app registrations, no OAuth. Nothing leaves your PC except what Claude Code sends to its model, update checks to GitHub, and, while AI drafts are on, what Clippy sends to Anthropic (see Outbound connections).
  • Never indexes attachment contents. Only file names.
  • Never touches your Claude credentials. AI drafts run your own signed-in Claude Code, or an API key you type in. Clippy never reads Claude Code's stored sign-in.

items.title: Network
items.text:
• Localhost only. The server binds to 127.0.0.1 and nothing else. Other computers on your network can't reach it. It does not bind to the WSL virtual adapter either, which is why WSL needs mirrored networking.
  • Bearer token. Every request must carry Authorization: Bearer <token>. The comparison is constant-time. Requests without a valid token get an empty 401.
  • Token storage. The token is stored encrypted with Windows DPAPI for your Windows user, in %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\token.bin. It is never written to settings.json or to logs. Regenerate it any time from the tray. If you save an Anthropic API key for AI drafts, it is stored the same way (DPAPI-encrypted) in %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\anthropic-key.bin; the file exists only if you save a key.
  • Browsers are blocked. Any request with an Origin header gets a 401, so a web page can't call the server, even from your own PC.
  • No OAuth prompts. The 401 carries no WWW-Authenticate header, so MCP clients don't start an OAuth flow.

items.title: Outbound connections
items.text:
Clippy makes exactly two kinds of outbound connection:

  • GitHub, for updates. Once a week (unless you set Don't check), the installed copy asks GitHub for the latest release and may download ClippysRevenge.exe and SHA256SUMS.txt. These are plain unauthenticated requests that send only a ClippysRevenge/<version> user agent. Nothing about you, your mail, the index or your settings is sent, and there is no telemetry. See Updates.
  • Anthropic, only while AI drafts are on. See AI drafts data flow.

All connections use HTTPS with normal certificate checks. Update downloads follow redirects only to GitHub's own hosts.

items.title: Update trust model
items.text:
An update is accepted when it comes over HTTPS from the project's GitHub release and its SHA-256 matches the SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release. This proves the file is the one published in the release and arrived intact. It does not prove who published it: whoever can publish a release in the repository (a stolen account or token, a compromised workflow) could publish a matching exe, and copies set to Install automatically would install it within a week without asking. Clippy starts only its own installed exe after an update, never runs a script, and rolls back a version that doesn't start.

If you want to review each release first, set Settings, General, Updates to Only tell me or Don't check. See Updates.

items.title: File access
items.text:
Every file path a tool reads or writes goes through a path policy. A path must be inside an allowed folder:

  • the attachment folder, %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Clippy's Revenge by default, which is always allowed
  • %USERPROFILE%\Documents
  • any folders you add in Settings, General

Paths with .., UNC paths, \\?\ paths, alternate data streams and junction escapes are refused. This stops a prompt-injected email from making Claude write into places like the Startup folder, or read files such as ~/.ssh. A refused path is shown as Blocked in the Activity window.

items.title: Index at rest
items.text:
The index holds message bodies as plain text, like Outlook's own cache (OST) file. It is protected by your Windows profile's file permissions and by your disk encryption. There is no extra encryption layer.

Turn on BitLocker

Without full-disk encryption, anyone with your disk can read the index.

items.title: AI drafts data flow
items.text:
AI drafts are the one feature that sends mail text off your PC. They are off by default and need your consent. While on, Clippy sends to Anthropic (through your Claude Code or your API key):

  • the email being answered, with its quoted history (cut at 20,000 characters)
  • up to 8 earlier messages of the same thread from the local index, your own text only
  • attachment file names, never attachment contents
  • your name and address, today's date, and your writing-style guide
  • once a week, about 150 to 300 samples of your sent mail for the style guide, with addresses, links and phone numbers removed

Nothing else from the index is sent, and shared mailboxes only if you turn them on one by one. The model gets no tools: it can't read files, search mail or run anything. Its answer is validated and cleaned to plain formatting and saved as a reply draft, never sent. Claude Code (or the API) and your Claude plan terms govern what happens to the data after it leaves Clippy.

Clippy never reads Claude Code's stored credentials and never signs in for you. Logs and the Activity window don't contain mail text, prompts, the style guide or Claude's answers.

The style skill is visible to Claude Code

The style guide is saved as %USERPROFILE%.claude\skills\my-email-style\SKILL.md, a user-level Claude Code skill, so your interactive Claude Code sessions (which have tools) can load it. Review it with View in Settings, edit it, or delete it any time. See Your writing style.

items.title: Statistics and SQL queries
items.text:
email_stats and query_index let Claude count and query the local index. They expose the same data that search_emails and get_message already return, and nothing else: no sync state, settings, AI decisions or internal ids, and no attachment content (only file names are indexed). email_stats returns counts and names, never mail text.

query_index is read-only through several independent layers, so that a mistaken or malicious query can't change anything:

  • The connection to the index file is opened read-only, with writing switched off.
  • Only three views (mail, mail_fts, mail_attachments) can be read. Every table, column and function access is checked, and anything else is refused, such as other tables, PRAGMA, ATTACH, loading extensions and every write.
  • One SELECT per call, no ? parameters, a 10 second limit, at most 1000 rows, and long text is cut at 2,000 characters.
  • The views are created for that one call and leave the index file unchanged.

It can't touch your mailbox in Outlook at all: it only reads Clippy's own index.

The text of a query (SQL), the values it returns and SQLite's error messages are never written to the log. See Logs.

items.title: Prompt injection
items.text: Email is untrusted text, and Claude reads it. Clippy limits what a malicious email could make Claude do: it can't send mail, can't delete mail, can only write files to allowed folders, and every meeting invite needs your click. AI drafts get a model with no tools at all, so the worst a malicious email can do there is produce a bad draft. Still, check drafts before you send them, and read the invite dialog before you click Send.

items.title: Logs
items.text: Logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\logs and kept for 7 days. They contain tool names, counts and errors. The token, the saved API key and any sk-ant-… or Bearer … text are masked, and mail bodies and search text are not logged. Activity events show subjects and counts only. The SQL of a query_index call and the text of a tool's error message (which can quote a search or a SQL error back to Claude) are not logged either, only the kind of error. Tool calls appear as the tool name, with counts and timings.

items.title: Unsigned executable
items.text: The release exe is not code-signed yet. The installer and the automatic updater check its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release before installing. That proves integrity, not the publisher. See Update trust model.

items.title: Tools reference
items.text:
Clippy's Revenge gives Claude Code twelve tools. You normally don't call them yourself: you ask Claude in plain language and it picks the right tool. This page lists every tool and its parameters, which is useful when you want to know what Claude can and can't do.

Tool What it does search_emails Search the local index get_message Read one email in full get_attachment Save one attachment to disk save_attachments Save attachments of all emails matching a search create_draft Save a new email draft reply_draft Save a reply draft list_events List calendar events find_free_times Suggest meeting times from free/busy send_meeting_invite Create a meeting (the only tool that can send) index_status Show index and sync state email_stats Count mail by sender, domain, folder or time query_index Run one read-only SELECT over the index

items.title: Common conventions
items.text:
• mailbox: empty means your own mailbox. An SMTP address means that shared mailbox, which must be enabled in the tray. Search tools also accept all. Tools that take an id find the mailbox from the id.
  • Dates: ISO date (2026-03-01) or date-time (2026-03-01T14:30), in local time. A date-only end date includes the whole day.
  • Recipients: "Last, First <you@example.com>; other@example.com". Separate people with ;, never ,, because names are often written "Last, First".
  • File paths: every path must be inside an allowed folder. See file access. Relative paths resolve under the attachment folder.
  • Errors: tools return a message that tells Claude what to fix.

items.title: search_emails
items.text:
Searches the local index. It is fast and works while Outlook is busy. All filters are optional and combine with AND. Results are newest first. Only synced mail is indexed; use index_status to check coverage.

Parameter Type Description query string Free text over subject, body, sender, recipients and attachment file names. Words are ANDed. Use OR between words for alternatives, "quotes" for a phrase, and a trailing * for a prefix. sender string Substring of the sender's name or email address recipient string Substring of To or CC. Also accepts a list like Ann <ann@example.com>; bob@example.com, which matches mail involving any of them subject string Substring of the subject date_from string Earliest date, inclusive date_to string Latest date, inclusive folder string inbox, sent, or another indexed folder path. Subfolders are not included. Empty means all folders has_attachment bool true: only mail with real (non-inline) attachments; false: only mail without attachment_name string Substring of any attachment file name attachment_ext string Exact attachment extension, with or without the dot (pdf or .pdf) unread bool true: only unread; false: only read mailbox string Empty, a shared mailbox address, or all limit int Maximum results, 1 to 200 (default 50) offset int Results to skip, for paging (default 0)

Each result has id, mailbox, folder, date (local time), from, sender_email, to, subject, has_attachments, attachments[] (name, size, inline flag) and snippet. Pass a result's id to get_message to read the body.

Example request

"Find unread mail from Ann with a PDF attached since 1 March."

Claude calls search_emails with sender="Ann", unread=true, attachment_ext="pdf", date_from="2026-03-01".

items.title: get_message
items.text:
Returns one email in full: headers, complete body and attachment list. It reads the index first. If the email isn't indexed yet, it reads it live from Outlook, which needs Outlook to be running.

Parameter Type Description id string, required The id of an email, as returned by search_emails

items.title: index_status
items.text:
Shows the state of the local index: per-mailbox counts, oldest and newest indexed mail, last sync and whether the first backfill is complete. It also says whether Outlook is running and what Clippy is doing right now. Use it to explain why a search found nothing, or to check indexing progress.

Parameter Type Description mailbox string Optional shared mailbox address. Empty means all configured mailboxes

items.title: email_stats
items.text:
Counts emails in the local index, grouped, in one call. Use it for questions such as "top 10 people who emailed me last year" or "how much mail do I get per month". It returns counts and names only, never mail text. It is read-only and fast, because the counting runs inside the index.

All the filters of search_emails work here (query, sender, recipient, subject, date_from, date_to, folder, has_attachment, attachment_name, attachment_ext, unread, mailbox), with the same meaning. There is no limit or offset.

Parameter Type Description group_by string, required What to group by. See the table below top int Number of groups to return, 1 to 200 (default 10) order string count: largest groups first (default). key: by key, chronological for month, week and hour, Mon to Sun for weekday include_cc bool For recipient and recipient_domain: also count CC addresses (default true) mailbox string Empty, a shared mailbox address, or all

group_by values

Value Key sender The sender's email address, lower case. name is the display name in the newest email of the group sender_domain The part of the sender address after the @ recipient Each To address, plus each CC address when include_cc is true. An address counts once per email. name is the display name seen in the newest email recipient_domain The same, by domain. A domain counts once per email folder The folder path month yyyy-MM week ISO week, yyyy-Www weekday Mon to Sun hour 00 to 23

month, week, weekday and hour use your Windows time zone. (unknown) means an email had no address. Any other group_by value returns an error that lists the valid ones.

The result is group_by, mailbox, total (matching emails, not recipient entries), distinct (number of groups), truncated (true when there are more groups than top) and rows. Each row has key, count, first and last (the dates of the oldest and newest email in the group, local time with offset), and name for sender and recipient.

With mailbox="all", the counts of every enabled mailbox are added together by key. An email that is in two mailboxes counts twice.

Example requests

"Who emailed me most in the last year? Top 10 with counts."

Claude calls email_stats with group_by="sender", folder="inbox", date_from one year ago.

"How much mail do I get per month?" is group_by="month", order="key". "Who do I write to most?" is group_by="recipient", folder="sent". "Which companies send me the most mail?" is group_by="sender_domain".

For joins, snippets or any other question that grouping can't answer, use query_index.

items.title: query_index
items.text:
Runs one read-only SQLite SELECT over the local email index. Use it for questions the other tools can't answer in one call: joins, custom grouping and full-text search with snippets. For plain counts, email_stats is simpler. It works while Outlook is busy or closed, and only synced mail is indexed.

Parameter Type Description sql string, required One SELECT (WITH and VALUES also work). Write values into the SQL; ? parameters are not supported mailbox string Empty, a shared mailbox address, or all max_rows int Maximum rows returned, 1 to 1000 (default 200)

Views. The query sees exactly these three views, which hold the same data that search_emails and get_message return.

View Columns mail id (the id that get_message takes), doc (join key), mailbox (empty for your own), folder, date (local time, yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss), unix_time (UTC seconds), sender_name, sender_email, to_addrs, cc_addrs (Name <email>; ...), subject, topic (conversation topic), body (plain text), unread (0 or 1), has_attachments (0 or 1, not counting inline images), attachment_names (one file name per line) mail_fts The full-text index: mail_fts (use it with MATCH, snippet(), highlight()), rank, doc, subject, body, sender_name, sender_email, to_addrs, cc_addrs, attachment_names. Join to mail on doc mail_attachments doc, position, filename, size, is_inline (0 or 1). Only file names are indexed, never attachment content

For full-text search, filter with WHERE mail_fts MATCH '...' (FTS5 syntax: words are ANDed, OR, NOT, "a phrase", prefix*, column:word) and sort with ORDER BY rank. snippet(mail_fts, n, ...) and highlight(mail_fts, n, ...) take a column number: 0 subject, 1 body, 2 sender name, 3 sender email, 4 To, 5 CC, 6 attachment names.

Limits

  • One statement only. PRAGMA, ATTACH, every write and every other table are refused, with an error that names what was not allowed.
  • 10 seconds in total, at most 1000 rows (max_rows), at most 100 columns, and long text cells are cut at 2,000 characters. On a large mailbox add a LIMIT and a date or folder filter.
  • With mailbox="all" each mailbox is queried separately and the rows are joined with a leading mailbox column. Counts and other aggregates are therefore per mailbox; use email_stats for counts merged across mailboxes.

The result has columns, rows (numbers stay numbers, empty values are null), row_count, truncated, truncated_cells and elapsed_ms. When it stops early it also gives truncated_reason: max_rows or size.

Example queries

Top senders in your Inbox in the last year:

SELECT sender_email, count(*) AS n FROM mail
WHERE folder = 'Inbox' AND unix_time >= strftime('%s','now','-1 year')
GROUP BY sender_email ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10

Mail per month:

SELECT substr(date,1,7) AS month, count(*) AS n FROM mail
GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

Full-text search with snippets:

SELECT m.id, m.date, m.subject,
       snippet(mail_fts, 1, '**', '**', '…', 12) AS hit
FROM mail_fts JOIN mail m ON m.doc = mail_fts.doc
WHERE mail_fts MATCH 'budget AND 2026' ORDER BY rank LIMIT 20

PDF attachments by sender:

SELECT m.sender_email, count(*) AS n
FROM mail_attachments a JOIN mail m ON m.doc = a.doc
WHERE lower(a.filename) LIKE '%.pdf' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20

Read-only, by several layers

The query runs on a read-only connection to the index with writing switched off, and every table and column access is checked. Only the three views above can be read, not sync state, settings or anything else in the database. See Security.

items.title: Attachments
items.text: Attachments are saved with a live call to Outlook, so Outlook must be running. Files are never overwritten: a duplicate name becomes name (2).ext.

items.title: get_attachment
items.text:
Saves one attachment of an email to disk and returns its path, file name and size.

Parameter Type Description id string, required The id of an email, from search_emails filename string File name of the attachment (whole name, case-insensitive) position int 1-based position in the email's attachment list save_dir string Folder to save into. Empty means the attachment folder. Relative paths go under it. Must be inside an allowed folder

If the email has more than one attachment, pass filename or position. If you pass neither, the error lists the attachments so Claude can choose.

items.title: save_attachments
items.text:
Finds emails with the same filters as search_emails and saves their attachments into one folder. attachment_name and attachment_ext also choose which attachments are saved. Inline images are skipped unless include_inline is true. Returns saved[], failed[] and count. One failure doesn't stop the rest.

Parameter Type Description save_dir string Folder to save into. Empty means the attachment folder query, sender, recipient, subject, date_from, date_to, folder, has_attachment, attachment_name, attachment_ext, unread, mailbox Same as in search_emails include_inline bool true: also save inline attachments such as embedded images (default false) limit int Maximum number of emails, 1 to 200 (default 50) offset int Emails to skip, for paging

items.title: Drafts
items.text: Drafts are only ever saved to the Drafts folder. You review and send them from Outlook. Nothing is sent by these tools.

items.title: create_draft
items.text:
Creates a new draft. The default signature is added below the text when you have one set. Every attachment path is checked before anything is created; if one is refused, nothing is created.

Parameter Type Description to string, required Recipients, separated by ; subject string, required Subject line body string, required Plain text, or an HTML fragment when html is true cc string Same format as to bcc string Same format as to html bool true when body is HTML (default false) attachments string[] Full paths to existing files in allowed folders mailbox string Empty means your own mailbox, or an enabled shared mailbox. The draft goes to that mailbox's Drafts folder and is sent on its behalf

Returns id, subject, mailbox and signature_added.

items.title: reply_draft
items.text:
Creates a reply draft to an email. The body is placed above the quoted original, followed by your reply signature when one is set.

Subjects start with Re::

Reply subjects start with Re:: (a double colon). This is intentional.

Parameter Type Description id string, required Id of the email to reply to, from search_emails body string, required Plain text reply, or an HTML fragment when html is true reply_all bool true: reply to all recipients (default false) html bool true when body is HTML (default false) mailbox string Empty means the mailbox the original is in, or an enabled shared mailbox

Returns id, subject, mailbox and signature_added.

items.title: Calendar
items.text: See Calendar and meetings for how these fit together.

items.title: list_events
items.text:
Lists calendar events in a time window, with recurring events expanded into instances. Sorted by start, at most 500. Defaults to the next 7 days.

Parameter Type Description start string Window start. Default: today 00:00 end string Window end. Default: start plus days days int Window length in days when end isn't given, 1 to 366 (default 7) mailbox string A shared mailbox's calendar. Empty means yours

Each event has id, subject, start, end, all_day, location, organizer, is_recurring and busy_status. The result also has count and truncated.

items.title: find_free_times
items.text:
Finds times when everyone is free, from Outlook free/busy. Nothing is booked. Returns numbered suggestions (whole free blocks) with start, end, adjacent and a ready-to-show text, and offers: options of exactly duration_minutes, with offer_text ready to paste into an email. People whose free/busy can't be read (for example, people outside your organization) are listed in unknown_attendees and ignored.

Ranking. Times right before or after one of your meetings come first (within 15 minutes, on the same day), then times next to a tentative meeting, then everything else, each group in date order. adjacent says which: busy, tentative or none. Free/busy can't tell a meeting from other busy time, so "next to a meeting" means "next to busy time". Without your own calendar (include_me=false, or your free/busy can't be read), every time is none.

Offers. offers and offer_text hold at most max_suggestions options of exactly duration_minutes, in the same order, one per line:

1. Tue 11/18  10:00–11:00 PT  (19:00–20:00 CET)
2. Wed 11/19  14:00–15:00 PT  (23:00–00:00 CET)

With offer_cet=true (for someone in Europe) each line also shows the time in Central European time, always labelled CET, also in summer. Options between 08:00 and 18:00 CET come first. If there are fewer than wanted, the rest follow in a second list headed Outside European office hours:. Each offer has list: main or outside_hours. See Meeting times in AI drafts.

Parameter Type Description recipients string, required Attendees as Name <email>; Name <email> duration_minutes int Minimum free block length, 1 to 1440 (default 60) days_ahead int Calendar days to search, up to 60 (default 10) date_from string Start date or date-time. Default: now earliest_hour int Working-hours start, 0 to 23. Default: from Settings latest_hour int Working-hours end, 1 to 24. Default: from Settings business_days_only bool Skip Saturdays and Sundays. Default: from Settings include_me bool Also check the calendar owner (default true) max_suggestions int 1 to 20 (default 5). Also the most offers returned mailbox string Empty means your calendar, or an enabled shared mailbox offer_cet bool true when the person you are writing to is in Europe: offers also show CET, Europe office hours first (default false)

items.title: send_meeting_invite
items.text:
Creates a meeting and sends the invite. This is the only tool that can send anything. What happens depends on the invite mode in Settings:

  • Send: a confirmation dialog opens on your PC. The invite goes out when you click Send. You can instead save it as a draft or cancel.
  • Draft only: the meeting is saved in your calendar, unsent. You send it from Outlook.
  • Disabled: the tool returns an error.

Every recipient must resolve in Outlook, or nothing is created. If the result is cancelled, Claude is told not to retry unless you ask.

Parameter Type Description recipients string, required Attendees as Name <email>; Name <email> or bare emails, separated by ; subject string, required Meeting subject start string, required Local start date-time, e.g. 2026-03-01T14:30 end string, required Local end date-time body string Plain-text invite body location string Location, for example a room teams bool Requests a Teams link. See the note below mailbox string A configured shared mailbox to organize the meeting from. Empty means yours

Teams links

teams=true does not add a Teams link. Outlook's object model has no supported call for it, so the meeting is created without one and the result says so. Open the meeting in Outlook and click Teams Meeting if you need the link.

The result has status (sent, saved_as_draft or cancelled), a reason for drafts (user_choice, timeout or draft_only_mode), and a message for Claude.

items.title: Tray and Settings
items.text: Clippy's Revenge has no main window. Everything lives in the paperclip icon in the system tray (you may need to click the ^ to see hidden icons).

items.title: Icon colors
items.text:
The icon shows what the app is doing. Hover over it for a short description.

Icon Meaning Green Idle, or answering a tool call (brief pulse) Blue Indexing: pulling new mail, purging old mail, or the first backfill (animated) Grey Indexing is paused Grey with ! Outlook is not running, or not responding Amber Waiting for you to confirm a meeting invite Red Error. The tooltip gives the short reason

Double-click the icon to open the Activity window.

items.title: Tray menu
items.text:
Right-click the icon.

Item What it does Status lines Current state and email count, then the last sync time and when the next one runs Start Outlook Shown only while Outlook isn't running. Starts Outlook. This is the one place the app ever starts it Sync now Starts a sync cycle at once (disabled while paused) Pause indexing / Resume indexing Pauses or resumes syncing. The pause isn't remembered after a restart Rebuild index… Deletes the index and reads your mail from Outlook again. Asks whether to rebuild My mailbox or All mailboxes Shared mailboxes Check a mailbox to index it; uncheck to stop. See shared mailboxes AI drafts Submenu: Draft replies automatically (a check mark; asks for consent the first time), Draft a reply to the selected email, Show Drafts in Outlook (hidden while Outlook isn't running) and AI drafts settings.... See AI drafts Copy "claude mcp add" command Puts the full setup command on the clipboard Copy auth token Copies the token Regenerate auth token… Replaces the token after you confirm. Claude Code must be set up again Activity… Opens the Activity window Settings… Opens Settings Open log folder Opens %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\logs Open data folder Opens the data folder Start with Windows Toggles starting at logon About Clippy's Revenge… Opens the About window: version, update status, Update now and links to the documentation and release notes. See Updates Exit Quits the app

items.title: Activity window
items.text:
Shows the current state, a progress bar during the first backfill, and the last 500 events. You can filter by kind and by mailbox and copy the list.

Events show tool names, counts and subjects. They never show email bodies, search text or attachment contents. Event kinds are Sync, Backfill, Purge, Tool, Draft, Invite (shown in bold), Blocked (a refused file path or invite) and Error.

items.title: Settings
items.text: Open it from the tray menu. Changes apply when you press OK or Apply; Cancel discards them. If you launch the app a second time, it opens Settings in the running copy.

items.title: Connection
items.text:
• Port (default 8765, range 1024 to 65535). Changing it asks for confirmation, because Claude Code must be set up again. If the new port can't be opened, the server stays on the old one.
  • Token, hidden, with Show, Copy and Regenerate. Regenerating only takes effect when you press OK or Apply.
  • The full claude mcp add command, with Copy.
  • Test connection: sends a request without the token (expecting 401) and with it (expecting an MCP answer) and shows a check mark or a reason it failed. It tests the running server, not unsaved changes.
  • The .wslconfig snippet for WSL.

items.title: Index
items.text:
Pick My mailbox or a shared mailbox, then set:

  • Retention in months (1 to 120, default 12). Shared mailboxes can use the global value or their own.
  • Indexed folders: a tree of checkboxes. Default is Inbox and Sent Items.
  • Live statistics: email count, oldest and newest item, database size, last sync.
  • Rebuild.

Also here: add or remove shared mailboxes, and the global sync interval (30 to 3600 seconds, default 300).

items.title: AI drafts
items.text: Turns on and tunes AI drafts: the switch Draft replies to new email automatically, Use (Claude Code or an Anthropic API key, with Check and Save key / Remove key), Claude Code path, Model, Effort, Daily limit, Minimum confidence, Ignore mail older than (days), Only when I'm in To or CC, Offer meeting times when an email asks for a meeting with Number of times to offer\n(1 to 10), Never draft for and Only draft for (one address or domain per line), the mailboxes, and the writing style (View, Regenerate, Open in editor, Update weekly). A link at the bottom leads to the manual page that explains what is sent to Claude.

items.title: Scheduling
items.text:
These are the defaults for find_free_times and invites:

  • Work hours (default 8 to 17) and business days only (default on).
  • Time-zone label used in suggestions, such as PT. Empty means automatic.
  • Tentative counts as busy (default on).
  • Meeting invites: Send (with confirmation), Draft only, or Disabled.
  • Confirmation timeout in seconds (30 to 900, default 120).

items.title: General
items.text:
• Attachment folder (default %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Clippy's Revenge).
  • Allowed folders: where Claude may read and write files. See file access.
  • Start with Windows (default on).
  • Notify on errors (default on).
  • Log level (default Information). Applies at once.
  • Updates: Install automatically (default), Only tell me or Don't check. Check now opens the About window and checks for a new version at once. See Updates.

Settings are stored in %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\settings.json.

items.title: Notifications
items.text:
